title: Staged fallback using penalty-decay + graceful quarantine for regional failover and SLO enforcement
author: Asha Rao
description: Motivation: Recent multi-region incidents revealed two failure modes: (1) immediate global fanout when a region degrades which overloads remote capacity, and (2) rapid re-introduction of drained hosts because the routing feedback loop is too short. This PR implements a staged fallback policy with a per-host penalty-decay mechanism and a graceful quarantine mode to reduce cascading failures and preserve SLOs. Summary: - Introduces a StagedFallbackManager that routes requests along a 3-tier path: local -> regional -> global. Each tier has configurable thresholds and rate allowances. - Adds a penalty score to hosts that fail or exceed latency SLOs; penalties decrement via exponential decay (configurable half-life) to avoid permanent blackholing. - Implements a graceful quarantine that drains traffic from a host while allowing in-flight KV/cache warmups and KV cache transfers. Quarantined hosts are marked for background reconciliation and health-checked before rejoining. - Integrates with the SLO Enforcer: when error-budget windows fall below thresholds, the enforcer triggers earlier stage transitions and tighter circuit breaker thresholds. - Backward-compatible config: new fields added under runtime.fallback (see docs) with sensible defaults that preserve current behavior if omitted. Design highlights: - penalty-decay: configurable params {initial_penalty, decay_half_life_seconds, max_penalty}. Penalized hosts are deprioritized in routing decisions; penalty is numeric and can be exposed to the console for debugging. - staged policy: routes iterate through candidate pools; each pool has a soft ceiling and a hard circuit-breaker which will open only after consecutive windows of violations. - graceful quarantine: rather than immediately cutting traffic, hosts enter QUARANTINE_DRAIN state where only short-lived or priority requests are routed off; background transfer tasks attempt to warm KV cache on substitute hosts to reduce cold-start cost. - Telemetry: new metrics (fallback_stage_transitions, host_penalty, host_quarantine_state, quarantine_drain_success) and traces instrumented in the path. Rollout plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in this PR. 2) Canary in perf-canary with 2% traffic for 3h; monitor fallback metrics and token-level latency. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% if no regressions. 4) If SLO regressions detected, automatic rollback via canary script. Testing and validation: - Added deterministic unit tests for penalty decay math and staged transitions. - Integration test reproduces a simulated region-outage and asserts that global fanout is limited and host penalties decay as expected. - Load test harness scripts included (scripts/rollout_canary.sh) to automate staged ramp and alert thresholds. CI notes: initial e2e failed due to a mock timing issue (fixed with deterministic clock stub). All checks pass on the final run. Related work: ties into ENG-1842 (circuit-breaker refactor) and ENG-1897 (SLO Enforcer extension). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in description - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] console UI flags for ops - [x] docs/operational/fallbacks.md updated - [x] rollout script added - [x] feature flagged behind runtime.fallback.enabled Backcompat and migration: defaults preserve prior routing behavior; operators can opt-in to penalty-decay via the console or by flipping runtime.fallback.enabled=true. Monitoring: dashboards added under Observability -> Fallbacks; alerts for >10% fallback_stage_transitions increase over 5m. Notes: This is intentionally conservative in default thresholds to avoid premature host blacklisting. Future work: adaptive decay based on load, ML-driven penalty tuning, and exposing per-tenant fallback profiles.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can we expose a short debug view in the console listing host penalties? Ops requested quick visibility — Asha: Added fallbacks-config.tsx and metric host_penalty, will surface 10 most penalized hosts in the canary UI.

Evelyn Cho: Quarantine drain duration seems unbounded; we should add a max-drain timeout to avoid long tail capacity loss — Asha: Added max_drain_seconds with a default of 300s and a background forced-evict path after timeout.
Marcus Li: Suggest adding a unit test that simulates repeated flapping to ensure penalty doesn't oscillate — Asha: Added penalty_decay_test.go with flapping scenario and deterministic clock stub.
QA (Lena Park): Integration reproduced the previous fanout incident locally; verification passed and metrics look stable under the canary profile.
release_notes: Staged fallback and host penalty decay: adds a 3-tier fallback strategy (local/regional/global), per-host penalty with configurable decay, and a graceful quarantine mode to drain and reconcile hosts. Defaults preserve prior behavior and feature is opt-in. Includes telemetry and console visibility for operations.
notes: Hotfix label added after incident investigation; conservative defaults chosen to minimize behavioral risk. Ops playbook updated in docs.
